newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end mostly down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end mostly down.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly down on Monday on weak market sentiment, traders said.
The key January 1997 contract ended at 3,090 yuan ($372) per tonne, down 45 yuan. It opened at an intra-day high of 3,100 and hit a low of 3,085.
March fell 14 to 3,076, May 98 to 3,120, July 85 to 3,170, September 18 to 3,358 but November rose one to 3,398.
Combined volume fell to 17,100 tonnes from 20,300.
Traders said weak market sentiment dominated today's trading, resulting in falls in most contracts.
"The weak sentiment made many investors expect soybean to fall further in the next few days," one trader said. "This made few investors want to buy."
Traders said that the overall outlook for soybean was not optimistic due to poor fundamentals.
"Maybe soybean can rebound on technical overselling in the next few days but it cannot change the long-term pessimistic market trend," a second trader said.
